bib.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention" (Declarative Attention, DA). Namgyu Ho, Huzama Ahmad, Woosung Koh (equal), Se-Young Yun, Tal Schuster, Cicero Nogueira dos Santos. KAIST AI and Google DeepMind (Google authors advisory only). arXiv:2609.02737v2, 14 Oct 2026, preprint. 43 pages. Note: the footnote says v2 numbers are three-run means and differ from v1.

COVERAGE: I read the whole extraction (2149 lines), main text, limitations (Sec 8), appendices A-H and the prompts. I skimmed the reference list (lines 754-1049) for origins only. I read the qualitative traces (App F) lightly. Figures are known only from captions and embedded numbers; I did not view images. Page numbers below are PDF pages (about 12 pages main text) and the extraction line numbers are given as "L".

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. DA cuts attended KV tokens zero-shot at small accuracy cost.
 number: -45.8% (Gemma-4-31B), -19.6% (Qwen-3.6-27B); accuracy -1.40pp and -2.10pp
 setup: no training, one prompt. Thinking mode off. 15 long-context sources (RULER, LongBench v1/v2, LooGLE, ZeroSCROLLS), up to 128 examples each, 8K max generation. Means of 3 runs. B200, vLLM 0.29. Macro-averaged over sources. The 15-source suite was selected as the sources where DA works (see claim 10).
 quote: "DA reduces total average attended tokens by 45.8% on Gemma-4-31B and 19.6% on Qwen-3.6-27B, with average accuracy drops of 1.40pp and 2.10pp respectively."
 where: Table 2, p6, L277-279. Raw: attended tokens 13.84M -> 7.49M (Gemma), 22.34M -> 17.88M (Qwen). Accuracy 86.49 -> 85.09 and 84.92 -> 82.83.
2. The saving comes from the mask, not the prompt. The DA prompt alone makes the model generate more.
 number: DA-no-mask attends +50.2% (Gemma) and +35.2% (Qwen) vs vanilla. Mask cuts 62.9% and 40.7% relative to DA-no-mask. DA attends 48.6±0.2% and 52.7±0.4% of previous tokens. The mask accounts for the whole accuracy drop (1.93pp Gemma, 2.05pp Qwen).
 setup: same as claim 1. DA-no-mask uses the DA prompt with full causal attention. Decode steps +38% (Gemma) and +32% (Qwen) vs vanilla.
 quote: "The prompt format alone costs no accuracy, but its 17–38% longer generations raise attended tokens 50.2% above vanilla on Gemma and 35.2% on Qwen. The mask turns this overhead into a net saving, cutting attended tokens per response by 62.9% and 40.7% relative to DAnm."
 where: p6, L293-299; Fig 2 p7.
3. Measured per-step decode time falls with mask ratio, with up to 55% on Gemma and 31% on Qwen. Low mask ratios cost a little.
 number: overhead {3.5%, 3.9%} in the lowest bin (0-10%), saving {10%, 14%} at 60-70%, {55%, 31%} above 90% (Gemma, Qwen).
 setup: one B200, bf16, vLLM 0.29.0. 5 batches per task sized to about 80% of the KV pool, concurrency 9-54 (Gemma) and 10-111 (Qwen). DA and vanilla steps paired by batch and step index, at most 512 tokens. DA time includes block-table rewrite and host state machine. Equal-weight macro over tasks.
 quote: "an overhead of {3.5%, 3.9%} in the lowest bin, a saving of {10%, 14%} at 60 to 70%, and {55%, 31%} above 90%."
 where: p8 (Sec 5.2), L401-405; Table 11 p32. The authors say the settings may overstate low-batch on-device savings and understate the large-batch long-context target. The micro average gives 71.7% for Gemma above 90%, from only 10 tasks and 2,779 steps.
4. Net full-response decode time (roofline) is 0.76x (Gemma) and 0.87x (Qwen) of vanilla. Prefill is excluded.
 number: Gemma 276.2 ms -> 211.2 ms. Qwen 303.9 -> 265.2 ms. Global KV read is 73% (Gemma) and 86% (Qwen) of vanilla decode. Across the three runs the ratio spans 0.71-0.87 (Gemma) and 0.78-1.01 (Qwen).
 setup: roofline estimate on a B200 (2.25 PFLOPS bf16, 8 TB/s HBM) at 40% MFU and 70% MBU. Large-batch disaggregated-serving assumption. Charges DA's extra decode steps. It is an estimate, not a measurement.
 quote: "The roofline estimate puts DA's decode time at 0.76× of vanilla on Gemma and 0.87× on Qwen."
 where: Table 3 p9, L468-476; derivation in App C.5 p26-27. Table 3 cells: Gemma vanilla matmul 23.2 ms, global 202.5 ms, local 50.5 ms. DA: 32.0, 109.6, 69.6 ms.
5. Why the global KV read dominates decode (useful for the notes). Weights are loaded once per step and shared across the batch. Attention reads cannot be shared, so each sequence rereads its own cache and the read stays memory-bound.
 number: at a 1M-token context, global attention is 94.11% (Kimi-K3) to 99.37% (Qwen-3.6-27B) of a decode step for full-attention models. Indexer-sparse models are 56.49% (GLM-5.3-Flash), 66.55% (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), 83.22% (DeepSeek-V4-Flash). The share falls sharply with context: at 128K it is 14-20% for GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, and 89.54% for Gemma-4-31B.
 setup: roofline, single B200, MFU 40% / MBU 70%, each model at its vendor's KV dtype. A ceiling estimate that ignores prefill, assumes saturated batch, and was computed by the authors from published configs (Table 8). The share spans 54.4-99.59% over the MFU/MBU range tested.
 quote: "The global read is 94.11 to 99.37% of the step for the full-attention models above the rule and 56.49 to 97.50% for the indexer-based designs below it."
 where: Table 8 p28; Table 9 p29. Related worked example: Gemma KV bytes per token 81,920 B, 10 global layers. The intro says "15 GB of FP8 KV cache must be loaded per sequence at every decoding step for a 1M-token context" in Qwen-3.5-397B-A17B (p2).
6. Accuracy gap closes with scale. Token savings do not follow a clean trend.
 number: relative accuracy 29% (Gemma-4-E4B) -> 98% (31B). 64% (Qwen-3.5-4B) -> 98% (Qwen-3.6-27B). Focus success rate 58% (E4B) -> 98.7% (31B), and 89% -> 98.8% for Qwen. Gemma-4-12B attended tokens reach 183% of vanilla because 6% of responses do not terminate (98% excluding them).
 setup: single runs except the two largest models. Zero-shot, non-thinking.
 quote: "DA's accuracy relative to vanilla rises monotonically with model size in both families, from 29% at Gemma-4-E4B to 98% at Gemma-4-31B, and from 64% at Qwen-3.5-4B to 98% at Qwen-3.6-27B"
 where: p7 (Fig 3), p10-11 (Fig 7), Table 10 p30.
7. Absolute saving grows with context, since DA attends a roughly constant fraction.
 number: about 1M tokens saved per response at short context -> about 19M in the longest bin. DA attends about 49-63% of vanilla in every context bin. Relative accuracy stays within about 2pp up to 64K and falls to about 95% in the longest bin (Gemma).
 setup: Gemma-4-31B, pooled over 15 sources, three-run means. On Qwen, accuracy falls further (to about 93% of vanilla) and the saving shrinks at long context because Qwen uses global mode more (about 48% and 46% of tokens in the two longest buckets, against about 30% on Gemma).
 quote: "DA's absolute token saving grows with context (Figure 4b), from about 1M tokens at short context to about 19M in the longest bin."
 where: p8 L388-396; Fig 4, 9, 10, 11.
8. Most generated tokens run in cheap modes, and global steps bound the saving.
 number: on Gemma, <global> is about 26% of generated tokens. A <focus> step attends about 11% and a <local> step about 6% of what a vanilla step attends. Focus and local save 76-99% per token. Global steps are over 80% of DA's attended tokens.
 setup: Gemma-4-31B, 15 tasks, mode mix chosen by the model under the zero-shot prompt.
 quote: "On average, a <focus> step attends to about 11% of the tokens a vanilla step attends to, and a <local> step to about 6%."
 where: p10 Sec 6.2; p13 "Global mode costs".
9. DA composes with a sparse-attention indexer (DSA) at the per-step level but not in total scan, with the zero-shot step overhead as the cause.
 number: per-step indexer scan 0.46 of vanilla. Decode steps 2.78x. Total scan 1.28x (DA-no-mask 3.30x). Accuracy: vanilla 79.1%, DA 82.1%, DA-no-mask 84.9%.
 setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (41 global layers, 21 with top-512 lightning indexer), 2x B200, TP2, FP8, 131K window, 1,592 questions per condition, XML-inline chunks. Scan counts are reconstructed from responses and count candidate positions, not slots read. The DA prompt without the mask already causes 2.62x steps.
 quote: "Relative to vanilla DSA, DA is 3.1pp more accurate at 278% of the decode steps and 128% of the indexer-scanned tokens."
 where: p11 Sec 6.5; App G p39.
10. DA fails on some task shapes. The 15-source suite is selected.
 number: Gemma-4-31B on 6 outside sources: accuracy drop of 30pp (RULER/cwe 100.0 -> 70.3) and 21pp (structured_data 68.4 -> 47.4). Also attended tokens rise above vanilla on the output-length-grows tasks (e.g. fwe 3.22M -> 6.16M). Per-step attention still falls 39-67%. "15 of the 21 sources we report" work.
 setup: Gemma only. RULER qa_1/qa_2 skipped because the hard-coded prompt forbids reasoning.
 quote: "Accuracy collapses (−30/−21 pp) even as per-step attention drops."
 where: App E.3, Table 12, p32-33.
11. Segment format and boundaries matter modestly.
 number: format spread 2.6pp (Gemma) and 3.7pp (Qwen). Fixed-length token cuts change accuracy by +0.4pp (Gemma) and -1.7pp (Qwen). Differences under about 1pp are within run noise.
 setup: Table 4, single runs apart from the main rows. The tool-call transcript format was chosen.
 where: p11 Sec 6.4.
12. Mechanism, as the paper describes it. A finite-state machine over the output stream parses <global>/<focus magic_chunks="K">/<local> tags. It edits vLLM block tables, with no kernel change. Kept spans are rounded outward to 16-32-token blocks. The mask applies only to global-attention layers. Sliding-window (SWA) and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers are untouched. Always attended: the first 16 tokens (sink), the question plus instruction, and the response so far. Context is cut into about 2K-token "magic chunks" (target 2048, hard cap 2560). The cache is never evicted, so a later global step can re-attend anything.
 where: p3-4, App B p24-25.
13. Speculative ideas (not tested): reversible context compaction and "system-2" KV-cache offload, plus stacking with speculative decoding. Offload would prefetch out-of-focus segments when a declaration names them. Sec 8.3-8.4, p13-14.

LIMITS
- Zero-shot only. There is no training, and the authors call the results "a floor rather than a ceiling".
- Thinking mode is disabled because models "fail to follow the DA protocol within thinking tags" (preliminary, not reported). All evaluation is non-thinking.
- Long outputs: DA runs about a third more decode steps. Under DSA this made the total scan rise (1.28x).
- Fixed-context benchmarks with artificial segments. The agentic claims (segments from tool calls) are argued, not tested.
- Selected suite. The 15 sources are those where DA works. Six outside sources fail.
- Wall-time was measured per step, only on B200 with vLLM, and only for 512-token windows. End-to-end speedup is roofline-estimated, not measured. The measured saving is in a middle batch regime, not the large-batch disaggregated target.
- GDN state on Qwen still summarizes the masked segments, so the mask limits global reads, not all access to context.
- <local> can hallucinate. Prefill KV entries carry information from the full context, so the model may wrongly believe it can recall masked content (Fig 19, Ex 8).
- Compared against Quest, H2O or SnapKV: no matched-budget comparison. The authors say it would compare "an attention kernel to a protocol".
- Judge is Qwen-3.5-4B with a rubric from Gemini-3-Flash. Agreement with Gemini-3.1-Pro is 98.5% (kappa 0.94). Four sources use synthetic QA from Gemini-3-Flash.
- Most results come from single runs apart from the two headline models (3 runs). Qwen savings varied across runs: 31.1%, 5.8%, 21.9%.
- The attended-token metric counts KV positions, not bytes. Block rounding adds a few percent (not modeled in the roofline).
- Sep-Oct 2026 model names are the paper's own (Gemma-4, Qwen-3.6, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3). I did not verify them. I read no code in the paper beyond the prompts.

BUILDS ON
- Jin et al. 2024, Self-Selected Attention Span (trained per task, 7B, contexts up to 2K). Closest prior work.
- Sparse and dynamic attention at decode: Quest (Tang et al. 2024), SparQ, Double Sparsity, InfLLM, ClusterKV, TidalDecode, Native Sparse Attention, DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DeepSeek-AI 2025b, 2026).
- Eviction: H2O (Zhang et al. 2023), StreamingLLM / attention sink (Xiao et al. 2024b), SnapKV, FastGen, Scissorhands.
- Chain-of-thought (Wei et al. 2022); System 2 Attention (Weston and Sukhbaatar 2023); ReAct, Self-RAG, MemGPT; GazeVLM; ThinKV.
- Inference foundation: PagedAttention/vLLM (Kwon et al. 2023), FlashAttention (Dao et al. 2022), roofline (Williams et al. 2009), MFU/MBU (Chowdhery et al. 2023; Agarwal et al. 2023), disaggregated serving (Zhong et al. 2024; Patel et al. 2024).

CODE
Per-mode syntax (App H / Sec 2, p3). Repo: github.com/itsnamgyu/declarative-attention.
 <global>I need the founding year... Magic Chunk 2...</global>
 <focus magic_chunks="2">"Acme Corp was founded in 2003 in San Jose."</focus>
 <local>2011 - 2003 = 8 years.</local>
 <answer>8 years</answer>
Roofline formulas, App C.5 p26. Global time = A * b_kv / (8 TB/s * 0.70). Matmul time = 2*P*D / (2.25 PFLOPS * 0.40). Local time = D * s_local / (8 TB/s * 0.70). b_kv = 2 * L_global * n_kv * d_head * 2 bytes. Worked example: 13.84e6 * 81,920 B = 1.13 TB, divided by 5.6 TB/s = 202.5 ms.

FIGURES (captions)
- Fig 1 (p1): the three-mode mask over 12 chunks. Prompt 25,466 tokens; attended prompt tokens fall to 3,435 (86.5% reduction) and then 1,124 (95.6%). Explains the idea fastest.
- Fig 2 (p7): relative accuracy, decode steps and attended tokens for vanilla, DA and DA-no-mask. Shows that the saving is the mask.
- Fig 3 (p7): accuracy vs model size.
- Fig 4 (p8): accuracy and absolute token saving vs context length.
- Fig 5 (p8): measured wall-time saving vs mask ratio. Good for the notes.
- Fig 6 (p10): mode share and per-token savings by context length.
- Fig 7 (p11): focus success rate and attempts by model size.
- Fig 20 (p39): DA on DeepSeek Sparse Attention.
- Table 8 (p28) and Table 7 (p27) give the KV bytes per token and attention share of decode time across models, which is useful for the inference note regardless of DA.

PROBLEMS
- The extraction is clean text. Some table cells and figure bar values were reconstructed from garbled lines; every number quoted comes from table or prose text. I did not run the figures script or view images.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF text.
- The paper cites many 2026 models and papers I cannot verify. I report them as printed.
- Relevance for the target note: it fits notes/07 "Shrinking the cache" as a model-declared, non-evicting form of sparse attention (contrast with H2O, SnapKV eviction and Quest, DSA scans). The roofline and KV-share material (claim 5) also sharpens notes/08 or notes/01.
